subject: Test of Group Invariance with 3 Groups

messages.author: 4cd5e411135ab129
messages.subject: Test of Group Invariance with 3 Groups
parts:
Hi everybody,
I am running a test of group invariance in a path model with three groups, and I get different results when I reorder the groups. For instance, the path of a given covariate to a manifest variable is as follows
Group A: (B =  -0.074)
Group B:  (B =  0.024) 
Group C:  (B =  0.220)
The test of group invariance gives the following results
lhs op rhs X2 df p.value
33 .p17. == .p81. 0.324 1 0.569 34 .p17. == .p145. 4.176 1 0.041
I presume that 
p.value 0.569 stands for the comparison between Groups A and B (i.e., -0.074 vs. 0.024) 
p.value 0.041 stands for the comparison between Groups A and C (i.e., -0.074 vs. 0.220) 

If I reordered the groups, I get the following path coefficients (which fully correspond to the above coefficients)
Group A (previously Group B):  B =  0.024
Group B (previously Group A):  B = -0.074 
Group C (previously Group C):  B =  0.220
The test of group invariance now gives the following results
lhs op rhs X2 df p.value
33 .p17. == .p81. 2.834 1 0.092 
34 .p17. == .p145. 4.176 1 0.041 
Based on the above logic 
p.value 0.092 compares reordered Groups A and B (i.e., 0.024 vs. -0.074) 
p.value 0.041 compares reordered Groups A and C (i.e., 0.024 vs. 0.220) 

But it seems that this is not the case.  The p-values do not correspond to the path coefficients. Obviously, I missed a piece of critical information about how comparisons are conducted, but I could not find any hint about this issue. Any hint or help will be much appreciated.
Thanks for your consideration.

messages.subject: Re: Test of Group Invariance with 3 Groups
parts:
How did you "reorder" them?  Changing their labels won't matter because lavaan assigns group numbers in the order they appear in the data.  You can override that default using the group.label= argument (see ?lavOptions).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics

Dear Terrence
Thanks a lot for your prompt reply and your willingness to give a hand in this problem. The three groups are coded with names, so, the group ordering in the dataset was done alphabetically.
The first groups was called "Aut", the second "Com" and the third "Rel". So, it was "Aut" (the first group, alphabetically ordered) which was compared to "Com" (the second group) and "Rel" (the third group). So, what lavaan does is to get the first group that it finds in the dataset (the "Aut" group) and compare it with the other two.
To override the ordering, and make the "Com" appear first in the group I used the following commands
df$newfactor <- factor(df$oldfactor, levels = c('Com', 'Aut', 'Rel'))
dfNew <- <- df[order(df$newfactor), ]

So the dfNew has ordered the same data with the "Com"  group being the first, and thus the reference group.
So, what I did in the next step was to rerun the lavaan model with the dfNew .


A. Test of group invariance with "Aut" being the reference group with df data frame


Part of the lavTestScore



B. Test of group invariance with "Com" being the reference group using the dfNew data frame


Part of the lavTestScore with the reordered group
Same chi-square but the x2 of the first group (Com) with the second group (Aut) now differs.
Instead, the comparison between the first group (Com) with third group (Rel) gives the same chi-square with the previously first group (Aut) with the third one (Rel).


As for the "group.label", I did not know that function. At any rate, it gives the same results with my own (less-clear) way of regrouping.
Kind regards
Athanasios Mouratidis
